title: Maximum Manhattan Distance After K Changes
summary: Given a string s with directions 'N', 'S', 'E', 'W', representing movements in an infinite grid, you start at (0, 0).
statement: Given a string s with directions 'N', 'S', 'E', 'W', representing movements in an infinite grid, you start at (0, 0). You can modify up to k characters. Determine the greatest Manhattan distance from the origin that can be reached by changing at most k characters to any direction. The Manhattan distance between points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is |x1 - x2| + |y1 - y2|.
constraints: s has 1–100,000 characters drawn from N, S, E, and W; 0 <= k <= len(s).
Change at most k directions, then follow the movements from the origin in order.
Return the greatest Manhattan distance reached at any prefix of the changed path.
hints: Manhattan distance is the maximum signed projection toward NE, NW, SE, or SW.
For each quadrant, greedily spend changes on moves pointing outside it while scanning prefixes.
Score an aligned move as +1; change up to k opposing moves to +1, then score remaining opposing moves as -1.
Each change improves a fixed projection by two, so changing the earliest opposing moves maximizes every prefix for that quadrant.
editorial: Each change improves a fixed projection by two, so changing the earliest opposing moves maximizes every prefix for that quadrant.

tests.explanation: Changing S to N produces prefix position (-1,2), whose Manhattan distance is three.
Changing opposing moves lets the path reach distance six.
